name: Custom Payload (Plugin Message)
desc: Sends a plugin channel message from server to client. Used for mod/plugin communication.
notes: Common channels: "MC|Brand" (server brand), "MC|AdvCmd" (command block update), "MC|TrList" (villager trades), "MC|RPack" (resource pack).

writeup.p: The clientbound plugin message. A channel name string (20-char cap) plus a raw PacketBuffer payload capped at 1048576 bytes. Vanilla channels include MC|Brand (server brand, sent once at join), MC|TrList (villager trades), MC|BOpen (book opening), and MC|AdvCmd (command block updates). handleCustomPayload dispatches by channel name; unknown channels are ignored. This is the standard bus for server-to-client mod and plugin communication.

handleCustomPayload branches on the channel: MC|TrList decodes the merchant recipe list into the open GuiMerchant, MC|Brand stores the brand string on the player, MC|BOpen opens the written-book GUI. The buffer is released in a finally block. Channel length is capped at 20 and the payload at 1MB, with an IOException on overflow.

Rise 5.99 PacketDebugger logs the channel name of every S3FPacketCustomPayload to chat via Rise.addChatMessage, as part of anti-cheat fingerprinting: the module also times keepalives and transactions. Reading MC|Brand is the standard server-identity read: brand strings identify Paper, Purpur, BungeeCord, and plugin stacks before a bypass picks a mode. Rise 6.x registers the class in the script API. The dedicated BrandDetector modules of the wider ecosystem (Flux, Lycoris) sit outside this corpus, so PacketDebugger is the only real consumer here.

Purely observational. The payload is server-controlled; a malicious server can send oversized or malformed payloads, but the 1MB cap and try/finally release keep the vanilla path safe. Clients read the channel and payload for fingerprinting, and nothing is sent back, so servers cannot detect the read. The detection value is the brand string itself, which identifies the server stack before a disabler selects a mode.

implementation.overview: The clientbound plugin channel. Rise 5.99's PacketDebugger logs every channel name to chat for anti-cheat fingerprinting, and the MC|Brand channel is the standard server-identity read. Rise 6.x only registers the class in its script API.
implementation.server_handling: ServerConfigurationManager sends MC|Brand once per join with the server mod name. EntityPlayerMP sends MC|TrList when a player opens a merchant and MC|BOpen when opening a written book. The channel table is per-connection; the vanilla client only receives S3F and never echoes it. The wire payload length is the remaining readable bytes, capped at 1MB.
implementation.protocol_notes: readPacketData reads the channel (20-char cap), then takes the remaining readable bytes as the payload buffer, rejecting anything over 1048576 bytes with an IOException. writePacketData writes the channel then the raw buffer bytes. The payload is channel-specific; parsers must know the channel before reading fields from the buffer.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Passive surface. The brand and channel names fingerprint the server stack; anti-cheats that send their own channels (version checks, telemetry) leak their presence through this packet. Clients never echo S3F, so the read is undetectable server-side. No anti-cheat in the corpus flags the packet itself.

modules.name: PacketDebugger
modules.purpose: Fingerprint the server's anti-cheat and network behavior by logging plugin channels and packet timing to chat.
modules.how_it_works: onPacketSend logs C0FPacketConfirmTransaction window id and uid with inter-arrival milliseconds, C00PacketKeepAlive key with inter-arrival milliseconds, and S3FPacketCustomPayload channel name via Rise.addChatMessage. The S3F branch catches clientbound payloads as they pass through the event.
modules.anti_cheat_notes: Logging only, no mutation, nothing flaggable. The timing output doubles as a manual check of server keepalive/transaction behavior.
modules.variations: None in the corpus. Rise 6.x drops the module and exposes the class through the script API instead.

modules.name: NetworkAPI (script API)
modules.purpose: Expose the packet class to Rise's JavaScript scripting API.
modules.how_it_works: S3FPacketCustomPayload is listed in the clientbound Class array of NetworkAPI.java (line 106).
modules.variations: 6.2.4 ships the byte-identical file with the Client-release2 path prefix.

implementation.general_hooks: Rise 5.99: PacketSendEvent. Rise 6.x: script API table.
implementation.client_variations: Rise 5.99 logs the packet through its event bus; Rise 6.x exposes the class to scripts. No client in the corpus cancels or forges S3F.
